metadata.title: AI Identity and Access

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for governing identity, authentication, and authorization for AI systems, models, agents, and AI-enabled services.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: AI identity management, model access control, agent identity, and research versus production AI environments.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Pattern defining how identities and access rights are assigned, constrained, and audited for AI systems and agentic components.

props.name: threat-framework
props.remarks: Provides adversary-centric context for credential misuse, privilege escalation, and unauthorized access to AI systems.

props.name: threat-framework
props.remarks: Provides AI-specific threat taxonomy for unauthorized model access, agent impersonation, and abuse of AI privileges.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.value: Unauthorized AI Access and Privilege Misuse
props.remarks: Threats where individuals, services, or agents gain access to AI capabilities beyond approved scope or intent.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.remarks: Threats arising from lack of clear identity separation between humans, AI agents, and automated services.

metadata.remarks: AI Identity and Access defines how identities and access rights are established and enforced for AI systems. This pattern exists to prevent unauthorized use of AI models, unsafe mixing of research and production access, and identity confusion between humans, agents, and automated AI services.

components.title: AI Identity Governance
components.description: Management of identities representing humans, services, models, and agentic AI components.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Distinct and auditable identities are assigned to humans, AI systems, models, and agentic components.

components.title: Model and Endpoint Access Controls
components.description: Authorization controls restricting who or what can invoke, fine-tune, or deploy AI models.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Access to AI models and inference endpoints is restricted based on role, purpose, and environment.

components.title: Environment and Role Segmentation
components.description: Separation of research, development, staging, and production AI environments with role-appropriate access.

implemented-requirements.remarks: AI research and experimentation environments are isolated from production systems to prevent unintended cross-impact.
